rule: C1 Symbol identity. Every definition has exactly one ID. Every reference to it uses that ID: a call in the defining file, through an import, a re-export, an alias or a `require` binding. | Elixir: aliases (lexical, in source order ...) resolve to the full module
notes: call_type convention (SPEC gives no Elixir mapping; Elixir has no methods and the `macro` type is defined only for C/C++/ObjC and Rust `name!`): every local, imported and remote call is direct, a call through a value is callback. Operators and special forms (`|>`, `=`, `case`, `fn`, `%{}`, `__MODULE__`) are language constructs, not calls. `MyApp.Util.dashes` is reached by a bare local call in its own file (util.ex:3) and by a fully qualified remote call from page.ex:8; `MyApp.Util.slug` through `alias MyApp.Util` (page.ex:5). Same ID everywhere (C1). `alias` is a module dependency, not a call.
